text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - Bunds and futures will seek to extend the record gains posted today after the DTB March Bund futures contract reached a new all-time record high at 103.00 and maintained the gains. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 102.94, up 0.28 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - British gilt futures ended higher, buoyed by the strong pound, which attracted overseas investors, and by steady domestic demand. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 113-12/32, up 15/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - The French 10-year bond future set a new historic contract high for the third straight trading day, then retraced to settle off its best levels. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 131.66, up 0.2 from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Debt markets languished in negative territory in late trade, with activity and turnover levels low and investors playing spreads between Italy and the UK. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 130.92, down 0.16 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - The prices of U.S. Treasury securities opened slightly higher as the mark slid in value against other major currencies. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 112-18/32, up 03/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.7 percent.
JAPAN - The Japanese bond market was closed today for a holiday. It will reopen tomorrow.

EUROBONDS - New issue activity picked up sharply with deals in a swathe of currencies and structures. Siemens launched its three-legged euro Eurobond, in francs, guilders and marks, raising around one billion Ecu in total. Sears Roebuck set a $300 million five-year bond. Rabobank issued a $250 million four-year deal. BayerVB set a 400 million mark 10-year Eurobond.
